content: Established photo and 3D body scanning workflows make capture instructions concrete and validate them before calculation. 3DLOOK documents hard failures for undetected bodies, wrong front/side orientation, and incomplete bodies, plus soft warnings for head tilt, hand placement, body-part issues, and selfie capture. Its front/side guidance requires head-to-toe framing, close-fitting clothing, removed shoes and obstructions, tied hair, front A-pose with arms away and feet apart, and side pose with legs together and hands clear. Styku likewise warns that a scan can complete while measurements remain inaccurate because of pose, clothing, movement, shadows, and setup. These support per-view, actionable preflight checks and retake guidance, not a generic success state. Sources: https://saia.3dlook.me/docs/ ; https://mtm.3dlook.me/assets/pdf/How%20to%20take%20photos.pdf ; https://www.styku.com/en-us/support-kb/why-are-my-scan-measurements-inaccurate-even-though-the-scan-completes-successfully
